glossary.def: Time a request waits for capacity before prefill starts. It grows steeply as utilization nears 100%, and it counts inside TTFT.
The slow end of the latency distribution, such as p95 or p99. Fan-out makes rare slow calls common at the request level.
A one-way HTTP streaming format (`text/event-stream`) used to deliver tokens as they are generated, with ids and reconnection support.
Attention where all query heads share one key and value head, which shrinks the KV cache and decode memory traffic at minor quality cost.
The mapping from a sequence's logical KV blocks to physical blocks in PagedAttention. Two tables can point to one shared block.
SGLang's radix tree over token sequences that stores KV so prefixes are reused automatically across calls.
In speculative decoding, the chance that a drafted token is accepted by the target model. It drives the expected tokens per target pass.
Storing weights, activations or the KV cache in fewer bits to save memory and bandwidth, at some quality risk that needs an eval gate.
Cached tokens over prompt tokens for provider prompt caches. On Anthropic, cache reads over input plus reads plus creation tokens.
An OpenAI and Azure request field that improves routing of requests sharing a prefix. It never pins a machine or guarantees a hit.
How long an entry stays eligible after its last write or reuse: at least 30 minutes on GPT-5.6+, 5 minutes or 1 hour on Anthropic.
A per-request vLLM value mixed into the first block hash so only requests with the same salt share prefix blocks, which isolates tenants.
A cache keyed on a hash of the normalised request plus scope and versions. It returns a stored answer only for an identical request.
A cache of vectors keyed on a content hash plus the embedding model and version, which saves embedding calls for unchanged text.
A duplicate request sent after about the p95 delay, with the first reply used and the other cancelled, to cut tail latency on idempotent calls.
The longest chain of dependent stages in a request. Latency is the sum along it, so overlapping stages shorten the total.

claims.text: ITL = (e2e_latency - TTFT) / (total_output_tokens - 1), and ITL is the same quantity as TPOT.
GenAI-Perf excludes TTFT from the ITL average and LLMPerf includes it, so their numbers do not compare.
If a request fans out to 100 servers that are each slow 1% of the time, 63% of requests see at least one slow response.
Streaming does not change total time. It lowers time to first response and avoids client timeouts.
Server-sent events use the text/event-stream type, and a comment line sent about every 15 seconds guards against legacy proxies dropping idle connections.
OpenAI's guide says streaming makes moderation harder because partial completions are hard to evaluate, and moderation scores arrive only after the full output.
Cutting 50% of output tokens may cut about 50% of latency, while cutting 50% of the prompt may give only 1% to 5%.
Llama 3 8B (32 layers, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, bf16) needs 131,072 bytes (128 KiB) of KV cache per token, which is 1 GiB at 8,192 tokens.
In vLLM V1 the default preemption mode is RECOMPUTE rather than SWAP, and preempted requests are recomputed when KV space frees up.
DeepSeek-V2 MLA reports a 93.3% smaller KV cache and 5.76x maximum generation throughput versus DeepSeek 67B.
MHA checkpoints can be uptrained to GQA with about 5% of pre-training compute, reaching quality near MHA at speed near MQA.
PagedAttention reports near-zero KV waste and 2x to 4x throughput at equal latency versus the state of the art at publication (2023).
vLLM prefix caching caches only full blocks and uses a reference count per block.
Orca reports 36.9x throughput versus FasterTransformer at the same latency on GPT-3 175B.
Sarathi-Serve reports 2.6x capacity on Mistral-7B (one A100) and up to 3.7x on Yi-34B (two A100) versus vLLM under tail-latency limits.

vLLM V1 enables chunked prefill by default whenever possible, prioritises decodes, and a smaller max_num_batched_tokens (for example 2048) gives better ITL while above 8192 is recommended for throughput.
vLLM block hashes combine the parent hash, the block tokens and extra hashes such as LoRA ID, multimodal hash and cache_salt, and eviction is LRU.
vLLM's default prefix-cache hash is sha256 since v0.11, and the docs warn that xxhash raises collision and leakage risk in multi-tenant setups.
SGLang RadixAttention reports up to 6.4x throughput versus state-of-the-art systems on structured LLM programs.
An audit of LLM APIs detected global cache sharing across users in seven providers, including OpenAI.
Speculative decoding gave 2x to 3x acceleration on T5-XXL with identical outputs, and expected tokens per step are (1 - a^(k+1)) / (1 - a).

vLLM docs say speculative decoding reduces inter-token latency under medium-to-low QPS memory-bound workloads, and n-gram and suffix methods give modest speedups without adding workload at peak traffic.
In vLLM's hardware table, FP8 W8A8 via llm-compressor is supported on Ada, Hopper and AMD GPUs but not on Ampere.
With kv_cache_dtype fp8 and no calibration all scales are 1.0, calibration with llm-compressor is recommended, and --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers keeps sensitive layers in the native type.
KIVI reports 2.6x less peak memory, up to 4x batch size and 2.35x to 3.47x throughput with 2-bit KV quantization.
On OpenAI GPT-5.6 and later the minimum prefix is 1,024 visible tokens, a cache write costs 1.25x, a read costs 0.1x (0.05x on GPT-6.1 Sol), and one write plus nine reads cost 2.15x versus 10x.
Anthropic multipliers are 1.25x for a 5-minute write, 2x for a 1-hour write and 0.1x for a read (0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, 0.025x on Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1).
Anthropic minimum cacheable sizes are 512, 1,024, 2,048 or 4,096 tokens depending on model, and shorter prompts run uncached with no error.

On GPT-5.6 and later prompt_cache_options.mode is implicit or explicit, ttl supports only 30m, up to 4 cache writes per request (implicit uses one slot), explicit mode with no breakpoints means no caching and no write charge, and prewarm tokens are billed at the write rate.
Azure models before GPT-5.6 return 400 if sent prompt_cache_options or prompt_cache_breakpoint.

Azure PTU-M deployments keep caching but, per the Azure prompt-caching page, have no breakpoints and no cache_write_tokens (as of 2026-10-13 the PTU sizing page says GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 Sol support breakpoints). On models that deduct cached tokens in full, cached tokens do not consume PTU capacity; GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6.1 Sol use normalized token accounting where cached input and cache writes do consume capacity at model-specific weights.

Doc sizing example: 1,000 RPM, 200-token prompts, 20-token responses, ratio 8 and 3,400 input TPM per PTU gives 105.88 PTUs at a 0% cache rate and 76.47 at 50% (80 after rounding to an increment of 5).
Anthropic breakpoints look back only 20 block positions, requests may carry up to 4 breakpoints, and an entry exists only after the first response begins.
In Anthropic usage, input_tokens counts only tokens after the last cache breakpoint, and cache_creation_input_tokens splits into ephemeral_5m_input_tokens and ephemeral_1h_input_tokens.
MCP 2026-07-28 says servers SHOULD return tools in a deterministic order, and tools/list MUST NOT vary per connection but MAY vary by authorization.

OpenAI caches live on individual machines, and traffic above about 15 requests per minute can overflow to machines without the entry and miss (Azure states the figure per prefix and prompt_cache_key).
APIM llm-semantic-cache-lookup uses score-threshold from 0.0 to 1.0 where lower is stricter, Microsoft suggests starting around 0.05 and warns above 0.2 may mismatch.
RedisVL SemanticCache uses distance_threshold in cosine distance units from 0 to 2 (tutorial sample 0.15) and a ttl (sample 3,600 seconds).
MCP 2026-07-28 cacheable results carry ttlMs and cacheScope (public or private), and input_required results are not cacheable.
A hedged request after a 10 ms delay cut the 99.9th percentile of reading 1,000 BigTable values from 1,800 ms to 74 ms with about 2% more requests.
